newsitem.title: UK: W.African crude oversupply hits April values - trade.
newsitem.headline: W.African crude oversupply hits April values - trade.

text.p: A Nigerian Bonny Light for next month loading traded at a 19 cent premium to international benchmark Dated Brent on Tuesday, indicating West African crude oversupply in March is feeding through into April weakness, traders said.
"There's no sign of West Africans getting better at all," a trader said. "The plan is for everyone to get rid of their cargoes as soon as possible and start over."

The price of the April 1-10 loader sold to a U.S. refiner was 39 cents below the March official selling price and follows sales on Monday of two cargoes of Qua Iboe at dated +17 cents for loading April 1-10.
Traders assessed Bonny Light for March loading at dated +15/+20 cents.

A cargo of Nigerian Pennington for loading end-March also changed hands on Monday at the equivalent of Dated +45 cents fob West Africa cents for delivery into Trieste, or 48 cents adrift of its March OSP.
A Bonny Light loading March 27/28 sold to a Med refiner on Friday at dated +29 cents, while a Forcados loading March 16/17 sold to a trader on Friday at Dated -20 cents.
Traders estimated that between 15 million and 20 million barrels of March West African remained unsold.

They said further West African barrels were likely to be offered into the Med by lifters desperate to shift cargoes. But good supply of North African sweets would provide competition and ready availability of Iraqi Kirkuk would add to the weak tone, despite the absence of prompt Urals.
"West African is stating to compete with North African sweets," a Med trader said.
"So you are seeing the Med starting to be a market for a wider variety of grades. It remains to be seen whether West Africans can really be as attractive on numbers."
"We are still seeing ridiculously low numbers," another Med trader said. "Practically the only good thing is that there are no unsold (Urals) cargoes on the water."

Sellers of Urals with late March cargoes were however reportedly nervous about the prospects of obtaining reasonable prices. One trader was reportedly attempting a back-to-back settlement involving a Urals and Kirkuk.
A Swiss-based trader was heard offering a 80,000 tonne urals at around Dated -90/95 cents but traders said the market remained at its last trade level of around Dated -$1.05.
